doc.name: A — diffusers catalogue, silk drapery, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: reed diffuser and oil
Category: diffusers
Shot programme: silk drapery
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are a commercial stills director briefing a diffusers capture. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the floating levitation in a silk drapery treatment.

SUBJECT. A reed diffuser and oil. Lock the product itself to the reference — no proportional drift, no invented branding, no cleaned-up typography. Everything else in the frame is your design decision.

CAMERA. Product suspended mid-air with no visible support and a soft drop shadow beneath. Shoot on a 105mm macro at f/1.2, framing for frame-within-frame using foreground architecture.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with tungsten practicals in frame carrying the warm layer. Stage the product on or against wet river stone, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a Portra-style palette with creamy skin tones and soft greens. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Emit one prompt, one paragraph, no framing text of any kind before or after it.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
